questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Limit State Design of Beams for Flexure
questions.text: Explain the Limit State Design philosophy of Reinforced Cement Concrete according to IS 456:2000. State the assumptions in the Limit State of Collapse in Flexure. Derive the stress block parameters: depth of neutral axis ($x_u = \frac{0.87 f_y A_{st}}{0.36 f_{ck} b}$), maximum/limiting neutral axis depth ($x_{u,max} = 0.53d, 0.48d, 0.46d$ for Fe250, Fe415, Fe500), and limiting moment of resistance ($M_{u,lim} = 0.138 f_{ck} b d^2$ for Fe415).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Limit State Design of Beams for Flexure
questions.text: Design a Singly Reinforced rectangular beam section of size $250\,\text{mm} \times 450\,\text{mm}$ (effective depth $400\,\text{mm}$) to resist a factored bending moment of $120\,\text{kNm}$ using M20 grade concrete and Fe415 steel.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Limit State Design of Beams for Flexure
questions.text: When is a Doubly Reinforced Beam section required? Derive formulas for compressive steel area ($A_{sc} = \frac{M_u - M_{u,lim}}{(f_{sc} - f_{cc})(d - d')}$) and total tensile steel area ($A_{st} = A_{st1} + A_{st2}$). Design a doubly reinforced beam of size $300\,\text{mm} \times 500\,\text{mm}$ to resist a factored moment of $220\,\text{kNm}$ using M25 and Fe415.

Explain the design steps for Shear in RCC beams according to IS 456:2000: Nominal shear stress ($\tau_v = \frac{V_u}{b d}$), Design shear strength of concrete ($\tau_c$), Maximum shear stress ($\tau_{c,max}$), and Shear reinforcement design ($V_{us} = V_u - \tau_c b d = \frac{0.87 f_y A_{sv} d}{s_v}$). Check for minimum shear reinforcement ($s_v \le \frac{0.87 f_y A_{sv}}{0.4 b}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Limit State Design of Beams for Shear, Torsion & Bond
questions.text: Define Development Length ($L_d = \frac{\phi \sigma_s}{4 \tau_{bd}}$) and mechanism of bond failure (Flexural bond vs Anchorage bond). Design vertical shear stirrups for a simply supported beam of span $6.0\,\text{m}$ carrying a factored UDL of $60\,\text{kN/m}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Working Stress & Limit State Design Philosophies
questions.text: Differentiate between One-Way Slab ($L_y/L_x > 2$) and Two-Way Slab ($L_y/L_x \le 2$). Design a simply supported One-Way RCC slab of clear span $3.5\,\text{m}$ supported on $230\,\text{mm}$ thick masonry walls carrying a live load of $3.0\,\text{kN/m}^2$ and floor finish of $1.0\,\text{kN/m}^2$ using M20 concrete and Fe415 steel. Check for deflection according to IS 456.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Limit State Design of Beams for Shear, Torsion & Bond
questions.text: Design a Two-Way Slab of size $4.0\,\text{m} \times 5.0\,\text{m}$ with corners held down (restrained against lifting) carrying a live load of $4.0\,\text{kN/m}^2$ using IS 456 moment coefficients $\alpha_x, \alpha_y$. Design torsional reinforcement at corners.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Design of Short & Slender Columns
questions.text: Classify RCC Columns based on slenderness ratio (Short vs Slender column $\lambda = L_{ex}/D < 12$). State the minimum eccentricity check ($e_{min} = \frac{L}{500} + \frac{D}{30} \ge 20\,\text{mm}$). Derive the ultimate axial load capacity formula for an axially loaded short column with lateral ties: $P_u = 0.4 f_{ck} A_c + 0.67 f_y A_{sc}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Design of Short & Slender Columns
questions.text: Design a short square column to carry a factored axial load of $1500\,\text{kN}$. Use M25 concrete and Fe415 steel. Design longitudinal steel and transverse lateral ties.

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Design of Isolated & Combined Column Footings
questions.text: Design an Isolated Sloped/Pad Footing of uniform thickness for an RCC column of size $400\,\text{mm} \times 400\,\text{mm}$ carrying an axial load of $1000\,\text{kN}$. Safe bearing capacity of soil is $180\,\text{kN/m}^2$. Use M20 concrete and Fe415 steel. Perform checks for: (a) One-way shear at distance $d$ from column face, (b) Two-way (Punching) shear at distance $d/2$ from column face ($\tau_v \le k_s \tau_c = 0.25\sqrt{f_{ck}}$), and (c) Development length.
